item.text: The continuation pass recovered direct primary/official material for all eight chapters. The most useful additions are: Bangladesh’s own 2023 cyber-threat and WMD-policy records for 1B; UN peacekeeping and Myanmar-border security records for 2B; the UN Special Procedures communication and WHO dengue response for 3B; direct EU and Freedom House election-period records for 4B; World Bank, IMF, BBS, and the Labour Ministry wage gazette for 5B; WHO, UNICEF, World Bank, and the official pension portal for 6B; a documented integrity null plus TIB’s 2023 household survey for 7B; and precise IMF/project/pension implementation records for 8B.

I completed a continuation pass across all eight chapters without scoring Sheikh Hasina. New evidence units and dispositions follow.

Repository persistence was blocked before filesystem access by `bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR`; therefore `research-ledger-manifest.json` could not be updated locally. The following IDs are the persistence handoff.

### 1B — Nuclear / catastrophic risk

- `BGD23-091` — Bangladesh’s UN mission stated in October 2023 that Bangladesh supported complete elimination of nuclear, chemical, and biological weapons. Direct ruler attribution is limited to official government policy. [Bangladesh UN statement](https://nypm.mofa.gov.bd/pages/static-pages/6952668035ce18e1c05a99e8)
- `BGD23-092` — Bangladesh’s 2023 cyber-threat landscape documented phishing campaigns targeting government and law-enforcement entities. This establishes national cyber-risk exposure, not Hasina’s personal conduct. [Bangladesh e-GOV CIRT report](https://www.cirt.gov.bd/documents/cyber-threat-landscape-2023)
- `BGD23-093` — An August 2023 government cyber alert warned of anticipated attacks against Bangladesh cyberspace. [Bangladesh Bank CIRT alert](https://www.bb.org.bd/mediaroom/notice/Situational-Cyber-Threat-Alert-from-BGD-e-GOV-CIRT.4.8.2023.pdf)
- `BGD23-094` — An IAEA conference record describes Bangladesh’s planned low-level radioactive-waste facility at Rooppur and its Russian-built reactor framework. This is institutional safety exposure, not evidence of a ruler-directed risk choice. [IAEA conference record](https://conferences.iaea.org/event/330/contributions/28866/)

**Disposition:** retain as exposure, official posture, and institutional-safety evidence; do not convert into a personal-risk claim. No Bangladesh-specific 2023 CBRN escalation was recovered.

### 2B — International peace and lawful security

- `BGD23-095` — Bangladesh was among the leading contributors of troops and police to UN peacekeeping in 2023. This is a continuing national policy and has direct PM-level public endorsement, but not proof of particular mission conduct. [Bangladesh Armed Forces Division](https://www.afd.gov.bd/un-peacekeeping/position-of-bangladesh-in-un-peace-operation)
- `BGD23-096` — At a May 2023 peacekeepers’ event, Hasina reaffirmed Bangladesh’s support for UN peacekeeping and women’s participation. [UN Bangladesh speech](https://bangladesh.un.org/bn/node/234140)
- `BGD23-097` — Bangladesh’s Home Minister announced strengthened Myanmar-border security and BGB alerting to prevent drugs, weapons, and new unauthorized entries. Attribution is ministerial/governmental, not a demonstrated personal PM order. [BSS report](https://www.bssnews.net/news-flash/126985)
- `BGD23-098` — The IMF’s December 2023 resilience facility supported climate resilience and climate-financing priorities, providing evidence of multilateral cooperation outside military activity. [IMF release](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2023/12/12/pr23440-bangladesh-imf-exec-board-concludes-2023-art-iv-consult-completes-1st-rev-ecf-eef-rsf)

**Contrary/limitation:** targeted searches did not recover a precise 2023 Bangladesh-Myanmar or Bangladesh-India military operation, border escalation, or ruler-directed arms-control decision. Retain the earlier evidence-short disposition, without treating missing aggression evidence as proof of peace.

### 3B — Domestic safety and protection

- `BGD23-099` — UN Special Procedures recorded approximately 10,000 opposition arrests, alleged disappearances, detention deaths, and harassment of activists’ relatives during the late-2023 election period. [UN communication, pp. 1–2](https://spcommreports.ohchr.org/TMResultsBase/DownLoadPublicCommunicationFile?gId=28715)
- `BGD23-100` — The same communication recorded at least eight BNP members reportedly dying in custody after 28 October, with no independent investigations launched. [UN communication](https://spcommreports.ohchr.org/TMResultsBase/DownLoadPublicCommunicationFile?gId=28715)
- `BGD23-101` — The UN communication recorded reported voter pressure, including threats involving loss of social-protection benefits. [UN communication](https://spcommreports.ohchr.org/TMResultsBase/DownLoadPublicCommunicationFile?gId=28715)
- `BGD23-102` — WHO documented Bangladesh’s dengue response: DGHS coordination, control rooms, repurposed hospitals, updated clinical guidance, surveillance, supplies, awareness, and vector control. [WHO outbreak report](https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2023-DON481)
- `BGD23-103` — The World Bank approved a $200 million urban-health project including dengue early warning, outbreak response, primary care, and services for approximately 2.5 million young children. [World Bank release](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/08/30/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-improve-primary-healthcare-in-cities)

**Contrary evidence:** the government disputed arrest totals and attributed violence to BNP actors; AP reported government estimates of 2,000–3,000 arrests versus much higher opposition estimates. [AP report](https://apnews.com/article/41ab22ccaa503bbf180939ca2c5918c7)

### 4B — Political freedom and authoritarian rule

- `BGD23-104` — Freedom House’s 2023 report records BNP rallies, disruption and clashes, Odhikar’s registration revocation, and allegations of violence, ballot stuffing, harassment, and arrests around the electoral period. [Freedom House](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2023)
- `BGD23-105` — The EU’s November 2023 EBA monitoring mission assessed garment-sector progress while identifying continuing shortcomings in expression, association, assembly, and civil-society conditions. [EEAS mission report](https://www.eeas.europa.eu/delegations/bangladesh/eu-eba-monitoring-mission-bangladesh-12-16-november-2023_en)
- `BGD23-106` — The U.S. May 2023 visa policy covered officials, party members, law enforcement, judiciary, and security personnel believed responsible for undermining Bangladesh’s democratic process. [U.S. State Department](https://www.state.gov/taking-steps-to-impose-visa-restrictions-on-individuals-involved-in-undermining-the-democratic-election-process-in-bangladesh/)
- `BGD23-107` — Odhikar’s 2023 report records low turnout and alleged voter manipulation in 2023 by-elections. [Odhikar report copy](https://www.omct.org/site-resources/legacy/Odhikar-Annual-Report-2023_2024-01-05-200113_tsaa.pdf)
- `BGD23-108` — The government’s contrary position was that the Election Commission was independent and the election process would be subject to official and international scrutiny. [Election-period chronology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Bangladeshi_general_election)

**Temporal disposition:** retain the January 2024 election only as a clearly labeled consequence of 2023 scheduling and campaign decisions, not as a 2023 event.

### 5B — Economic well-being

- `BGD23-109` — The World Bank’s October 2023 update reports extreme poverty at 5% in 2022, improved services, faster rural poverty reduction, and widening urban inequality. [World Bank update](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2023/10/05/structural-reforms-are-essential-to-sustain-growth-poverty-reduction-in-bangladesh)
- `BGD23-110` — The same update reports FY23 growth slowing to 6.0%, inflation and balance-of-payments pressure, energy/import constraints, increased government bank borrowing, and financial-sector vulnerabilities. [World Bank update](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2023/10/05/structural-reforms-are-essential-to-sustain-growth-poverty-reduction-in-bangladesh)
- `BGD23-111` — IMF’s 2023 review records reform progress but continuing pressure on the taka and reserves, recommending monetary tightening, exchange-rate flexibility, and fiscal restraint. [IMF review](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2023/12/13/bangladesh-2023-article-iv-consultation-first-reviews-under-the-extended-credit-facility-542460)
- `BGD23-112` — Bangladesh’s 2023 food-security statistics reported 21.91% of households experiencing moderate or severe food insecurity. [BSS report of BBS statistics](https://www.bssnews.net/news-flash/165809)
- `BGD23-113` — The Labour Ministry gazette set the garment-sector minimum wage at Tk 12,500, effective after the November 2023 wage dispute. [Bangladesh Labour Ministry](https://mole.gov.bd/pages/news/69403164c4774958d7b437e0)

**Disposition:** retain measured welfare, macroeconomic, and policy records separately. They do not independently establish Hasina’s competence or intent.

### 6B — Social well-being

- `BGD23-114` — WHO reported 69,483 confirmed dengue cases and 327 deaths by 7 August 2023, alongside a formal DGHS response structure. [WHO](https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2023-DON481)
- `BGD23-115` — The World Bank’s EARN project targeted approximately 900,000 rural youth, about 60% female, with skills, alternative education, employment, and entrepreneurship support. [World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/08/27/world-bank-helps-900000-rural-youth-in-bangladesh-with-better-employability-and-entrepreneurial-opportunities)
- `BGD23-116` — The official pension portal records online enrollment/payment infrastructure and 16,600 registrants with Tk 19 crore deposited by 5 December 2023. [Universal Pension portal](https://www.upension.gov.bd/Public/PensionBriefEn)
- `BGD23-117` — UNICEF’s 2023 humanitarian report records the March 2023 Rohingya-camp fire, which damaged 2,805 shelters. [UNICEF report](https://www.unicef.org/media/151381/file/Bangladesh-Humanitarian-SitRep-%28End-Year%29%2C-1-January-to-31-December-2023.pdf)
- `BGD23-118` — UNICEF reported the continuing child-marriage burden and its effects on girls’ health, education, and life chances. [UNICEF Bangladesh](https://www.unicef.org/bangladesh/en/child-protection)

**Contrary/limitation:** WHO describes high dengue risk and health-system pressure; the pension record shows rollout and early uptake, not durable coverage or social effect.

### 7B — Personal integrity and honesty

- `BGD23-119` — No reliable 2023 source establishing Hasina’s personal enrichment, concealed assets, family contracts, or direct financial benefit was recovered. **Disposition: retain as an explicit research limitation only; do not infer innocence or guilt.**
- `BGD23-120` — Transparency International Bangladesh’s 2023 household survey reports corruption affecting 70.9% of households between May 2023 and April 2024. This is institutional/service-delivery evidence, not personal integrity evidence. [TIB survey](https://www.ti-bangladesh.org/en/articles/research/7179)
- `BGD23-121` — The IMF staff report records six of seven structural benchmarks met and one delayed financial-law benchmark. This is an institutional implementation record, not evidence of personal honesty. [IMF staff report](https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/cr/2023/english/1bgdea2023003.pdf)
- `BGD23-122` — Government responses maintained that the Election Commission was independent and law-enforcement conduct lawful, while UN and opposition accounts disputed those positions. [Government position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Bangladeshi_general_election), [UN communication](https://spcommreports.ohchr.org/TMResultsBase/DownLoadPublicCommunicationFile?gId=28715)

**Disposition:** reject personal-enrichment, concealment, and ethical-character inferences not directly supported by evidence.

### 8B — Effectiveness and competence

- `BGD23-123` — IMF records six of seven structural benchmarks, two of three performance criteria, and three of four indicative targets completed by the first review. [IMF staff report, pp. 6–7](https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/cr/2023/english/1bgdea2023003.pdf)
- `BGD23-124` — The pension system had operational online registration/payment infrastructure and recorded 16,600 registrants by 5 December 2023. [Official pension portal](https://www.upension.gov.bd/Public/PensionBriefEn)
- `BGD23-125` — The EARN project established a defined government–World Bank program with a 900,000-youth target, female participation target, training, stipends, and alternative education. [World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/08/27/world-bank-helps-900000-rural-youth-in-bangladesh-with-better-employability-and-entrepreneurial-opportunities)
- `BGD23-126` — The World Bank health project specified facilities, maternal-care, hypertension-screening, dengue-warning, and outbreak-response components. [World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/08/30/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-improve-primary-healthcare-in-cities)
- `BGD23-127` — UN evidence of arrests, deaths, voter pressure, and absent independent investigations provides contrary evidence against treating state execution as uniformly successful. [UN communication](https://spcommreports.ohchr.org/TMResultsBase/DownLoadPublicCommunicationFile?gId=28715)
- `BGD23-128` — World Bank economic reporting records simultaneous development gains and implementation constraints: poverty reduction and improved services alongside inflation, import/energy constraints, financial vulnerabilities, and urban inequality. [World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2023/10/05/structural-reforms-are-essential-to-sustain-growth-poverty-reduction-in-bangladesh)

**Disposition:** retain as separate administrative, social-service, macroeconomic, and crisis-management records. Do not treat regime continuity or the 2024 election result as a single effectiveness outcome.
